answer: Each agent must post a bond before it can enter the task market; a random audit checks whether supposedly independent agents share control or coordinate bids, and proven collusion burns their bonds. This does not make identities impossible to fake: it makes each extra identity require more capital at risk. A dawn rush of disposable accounts can no longer create a cheap plume of votes or bids; attackers must lock funds and face a spiral of losses as audits catch them.
